entries.kid: The football field is 100 yards long, with an end zone at each end.
entries.full: 100 yards between the goal lines, plus a 10-yard end zone at each end; 53 1/3 yards wide.

entries.kid: The place where you score a touchdown.
entries.full: The 10-yard scoring area beyond each goal line.

entries.kid: Lines painted every 5 yards to show how far the ball has gone.
entries.full: Field markings every 5 yards, numbered every 10, with the 50-yard line at midfield.

entries.kid: The team with the ball. It tries to score.
entries.full: The team in possession, trying to advance the ball and score.

entries.kid: The team without the ball. It tries to stop the other team.
entries.full: The team not in possession, trying to stop the offense and take the ball away.

entries.kid: One of the 4 parts of a game.
entries.full: One of four periods of a game; 15 minutes in the NFL and college, 12 in most high schools.

entries.kid: The official who makes sure everyone follows the rules.
entries.full: The lead official; with the rest of the crew enforces the rules and signals calls.

entries.kid: Getting the ball into the end zone. Worth 6 points!
entries.full: Possession of the ball in or over the opponent's goal line; 6 points.

entries.kid: A kick after a touchdown for 1 extra point.
entries.full: A try after a touchdown: a 1-point kick (NFL: 33 yards, from the 15) .

entries.kid: A run or pass after a touchdown for 2 points.
entries.full: A try from the 2-yard line (NFL) worth 2 points instead of the kick's 1.

entries.kid: A kick through the posts. Worth 3 points.
entries.full: A placekick through the uprights; 3 points.

entries.kid: When the defense tackles the offense in its own end zone. Worth 2 points.
entries.full: A 2-point score for the defense when the ball carrier is down in his own end zone, among other situations.

entries.kid: One of the offense's 4 tries to go 10 yards.
entries.full: One play in a series of four; the offense must gain 10 yards in four downs to earn a new series.

entries.kid: When the offense goes 10 yards and gets 4 new tries.
entries.full: The first play of a new series, earned by gaining the necessary yardage.

entries.kid: How many tries are left and how far you still need to go.
entries.full: The situation: which down it is and how many yards remain for a first down (e.g. 3rd and 4).

entries.kid: The last try. Punt, kick, or go for it.
entries.full: The last down; teams punt, kick a field goal or go for it depending on the situation.

entries.kid: A long kick to give the ball to the other team.
entries.full: A kick dropped and kicked before it hits the ground, usually on 4th down, to improve field position.

entries.kid: The center passes the ball back to start the play.
entries.full: The backward pass from the center that begins each down.

entries.kid: The QB hands the ball to a runner.
entries.full: A direct exchange of the ball from the quarterback to another back.

entries.kid: A pass nobody caught. The play is over.
entries.full: A forward pass that hits the ground or goes out of bounds; the ball returns to the previous spot.

entries.kid: Bringing the runner to the ground.
entries.full: Stopping a ball carrier by bringing him to the ground; in flag football, pulling the flag.

entries.kid: When the defense takes the ball away.
entries.full: A change of possession by interception or fumble recovery (or on downs).

entries.kid: When a defender catches the QB's pass.
entries.full: A forward pass caught by a defender, giving his team possession.

entries.kid: When the runner drops the ball.
entries.full: A loose ball after a carrier loses possession; either team may recover.

entries.kid: The leader of the offense. Throws passes and hands off.
entries.full: The player who takes the snap and throws or hands off the ball; calls the offense's plays on the field.

entries.kid: Players who catch passes: wide receivers and tight ends.
entries.full: Wide receivers and tight ends, the primary targets of forward passes.

entries.kid: The player who runs with the ball.
entries.full: A back lined up behind or beside the quarterback; carries the ball and catches passes.

entries.kid: The lineman who snaps the ball.
entries.full: The middle offensive lineman, who snaps the ball to the quarterback.

entries.kid: Five big players who block.
entries.full: Five linemen (LT, LG, C, RG, RT) who block for runs and pass protection.

entries.kid: Linemen rush, linebackers tackle, cornerbacks and safeties guard receivers.
entries.full: DL rush and stop runs; LB tackle, rush and cover; CB cover receivers; S defend deep and support.

entries.kid: A game with no tackling. You pull a flag.
entries.full: A non-contact variant where defenders pull a flag from the ball carrier's belt.

entries.kid: A broken rule, shown by a yellow flag.
entries.full: A foul called by officials, enforced by yardage and sometimes loss of down.

entries.kid: Moving too early on offense.
entries.full: An offensive player moving illegally before the snap: 5 yards.

entries.kid: Kicking plays: kickoffs, punts, field goals.
entries.full: The units that handle kickoffs, punts, field goals and returns.

entries.kid: The imaginary line where the ball is.
entries.full: The line parallel to the goal lines through the ball's forward point; teams are on opposite sides at the snap.

entries.kid: A player allowed to catch a forward pass.
entries.full: QB, RB, WR and TE by number and position; linemen are ineligible downfield.

entries.kid: The clock for each quarter. It stops for some things.
entries.full: Stops on incompletions, out of bounds, timeouts and most penalties; first downs do not stop it in the NFL.

entries.kid: The timer for how fast the offense must snap.
entries.full: 40 seconds (25 after some stoppages); delay of game is 5 yards.

entries.kid: An automatic timeout at 2:00 in each half.
entries.full: An automatic stoppage at 2:00 of the second and fourth quarters.

entries.kid: When a ball stops in the end zone. The team starts at the 20.
entries.full: A dead ball in the end zone after a punt, or an interception there: placed at the 20.

entries.kid: The mix of players on the field, named by two digits.
entries.full: Number of RBs then TEs; WRs fill the remaining skill spots. 11 = 1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR.

entries.kid: A defense with five defensive backs.
entries.full: A sub package of 4 DL, 2 LB, 5 DB (a 4-2-5), the usual answer to 11 personnel.

entries.kid: One safety deep in the middle.
entries.full: A single-high safety look; Cover 1 and Cover 3 are the usual coverages from it.

entries.kid: Two safeties deep, split.
entries.full: Two-high safeties; Cover 2, Cover 4 and Cover 6 live here.

entries.kid: Hiding what the defense will really do.
entries.full: Showing a look pre-snap that differs from the coverage or pressure actually played.

entries.kid: Safeties moving after the snap.
entries.full: Post-snap movement of safeties (and sometimes corners) into the final coverage.

entries.kid: A long kick that starts each half and comes after touchdowns and field goals.
entries.full: A free kick from the kicking team's 35 (NFL) that starts each half and follows touchdowns and field goals. Since 2024 the NFL uses a format with the coverage team aligned close to the returners.

entries.kid: The player who catches a kick and runs it back.
entries.full: The receiving team's player who fields a kickoff or punt and returns it.

entries.kid: A short kick the kicking team tries to get back.
entries.full: A short kickoff the kicking team may recover after it travels 10 yards (or is touched by the receiving team). In the NFL it must be declared in advance.

entries.kid: Wave one arm, catch the ball, and nobody may tackle you.
entries.full: The returner signals by extending and waving one arm overhead; he may not be hit and may not advance the ball after the catch.

entries.kid: How referees show what happened, using their arms.
entries.full: Standard arm signals: both arms up for a score, arm forward for a first down, arms crossed in front for an incomplete pass, and many more for each foul.

entries.kid: A defender is across the line when the ball is snapped.
entries.full: A defender in the neutral zone at the snap: 5 yards. Contact before the snap is encroachment.

entries.kid: Grabbing a player to stop them.
entries.full: Illegally restricting an opponent with the hands or arms. Offensive holding is 10 yards; defensive holding is 5 yards and an automatic first down in the NFL.

entries.kid: Stopping a catch by pushing or grabbing.
entries.full: Illegal contact that restricts a player's chance to catch a forward pass once it is in the air. NFL defensive PI is a spot foul with an automatic first down; offensive PI is 10 yards.

entries.kid: The play clock runs out before the snap.
entries.full: Failing to snap the ball before the play clock expires (and some other delays): 5 yards.

entries.kid: A break that stops the clock.
entries.full: A stoppage a team calls to stop the clock. NFL teams get three per half; youth and flag leagues vary.

entries.kid: The ball is handed off and carried forward.
entries.full: A play in which the ball is advanced by running, usually after a handoff or pitch from the quarterback.

entries.kid: The quarterback throws the ball to a receiver.
entries.full: A play built around a forward pass to an eligible receiver.

entries.kid: Shows the score, the time and the down.
entries.full: Displays the score, quarter, game clock, timeouts, down, distance and the ball's yard line.

entries.kid: Where the offense lines up before the snap.
entries.full: The alignment of the 11 offensive players, named mostly by the backfield (I, singleback, shotgun, pistol, empty) and receiver sets (twins, trips, bunch).

entries.kid: A fullback and a tailback lined up behind the quarterback.
entries.full: Quarterback under center with a fullback and tailback aligned in a line behind him: a power-running formation.

entries.kid: One running back behind the quarterback.
entries.full: Quarterback under center with a single running back about 7 yards deep; also called Ace.

entries.kid: The quarterback stands a few yards back to get the snap.
entries.full: Quarterback aligned about 5 yards behind the center, usually with a back beside him, for a better view and more time to throw.

entries.kid: The quarterback is a few yards back with the runner right behind him.
entries.full: Quarterback about 4 yards deep with the running back directly behind, combining a downhill run game with shotgun vision.

entries.kid: No running backs: everyone spreads out to catch.
entries.full: A formation with no backs besides the quarterback, usually five receivers.

entries.kid: A player who isn't allowed to catch a forward pass.
entries.full: Interior linemen (NFL numbers 50 to 79) may not catch a forward pass unless they report as eligible and align at an eligible spot; they may not go more than a yard downfield before a pass beyond the line.

entries.kid: One player moving before the snap.
entries.full: One offensive player may be moving at the snap, parallel to or away from the line of scrimmage.

entries.kid: Players changing spots before the snap.
entries.full: Offensive players changing positions before the snap; afterwards all must be set for a full second.

entries.kid: A defender bumps a receiver too far downfield before the pass.
entries.full: NFL: contact by a defender beyond 5 yards from the line before the ball is thrown; 5 yards and an automatic first down.

entries.kid: Hitting the quarterback after he throws.
entries.full: Late, high or full-weight hits on a passer: 15 yards and an automatic first down.

entries.kid: An extra, dangerous hit.
entries.full: Excessive or late contact, such as hitting a player who is down or out of bounds: 15 yards.

entries.kid: A college rule against hits to the head.
entries.full: College football foul for forcible contact to the head or neck area, or with the crown of the helmet: 15 yards and an ejection after review.

entries.kid: A coach asks for a play to be looked at again.
entries.full: An NFL coach's request, by red flag, for a replay review. Two per game, a third if both succeed; a lost challenge costs a timeout.

entries.kid: Officials watch video to check a call.
entries.full: Video review of a play. Scoring plays and turnovers are reviewed automatically; late in halves and in overtime, the replay booth starts reviews.

entries.kid: Extra time when the game is tied.
entries.full: An extra period played when regulation ends tied. NFL rules change over time; content states the season it describes.

entries.kid: The name of the play the team will run.
entries.full: The huddle call: formation, motion, the play itself and the snap count, worded differently in each system.

entries.kid: Changing the play at the line.
entries.full: A change of play called at the line of scrimmage after reading the defense.

entries.kid: Throwing the ball at the ground to stop the clock.
entries.full: An intentional incompletion right after the snap to stop the clock; it costs a down.

entries.kid: The quarterback kneels to keep the clock running.
entries.full: Ending a play immediately with a kneel to run the clock safely, usually when protecting a lead.

entries.kid: A real game moment to make a call on.
entries.full: A decision point defined by down, distance, field position, score, clock and timeouts.

entries.kid: A run that starts one way, then cuts back.
entries.full: A misdirection run: the back steps away from the play, then cuts back behind pulling linemen.

entries.kid: Two blockers on one defender.
entries.full: Two linemen combining on one defender to move him, one usually climbing off to a linebacker.

entries.kid: A run that looks like a pass at first.
entries.full: The offense shows pass protection to draw the rush upfield, then hands off underneath it.

entries.kid: 4 linemen and 3 linebackers.
entries.full: A front with four down linemen and three linebackers (Will, Mike, Sam); linemen usually attack single gaps.

entries.kid: Which side of a receiver a defender lines up on.
entries.full: A defender's alignment inside or outside the receiver, which takes away routes that way and concedes the other side.

entries.kid: Each defender follows one receiver.
entries.full: Each defender is assigned a specific receiver and travels with him; usually paired with a free safety (Cover 1) or no deep help (Cover 0).

entries.kid: A lineman leaves his spot to block elsewhere.
entries.full: A lineman steps back and runs along the line to block at the point of attack, leading a sweep or kicking out an edge player on a counter or trap.

entries.kid: The path a receiver runs on a pass play.
entries.full: The path a receiver runs: a stem upfield, then a break at a set depth and angle, timed to the quarterback's drop.

entries.kid: Routes that work together so one defender can't cover both.
entries.full: Routes paired to stretch a defender high-low or across the field, so the quarterback reads one conflict defender and throws away from him.

entries.kid: A numbered list of routes.
entries.full: A numbered menu of routes. In one common tree: 1 flat, 2 slant, 3 comeback, 4 curl, 5 out, 6 dig, 7 corner, 8 post, 9 go; odd break outside, even inside. Numbering differs by system.

entries.kid: The deepest defenders.
entries.full: The two deepest defenders, free and strong safety. How many sit deep in the middle before the snap is the first clue to the coverage.

entries.kid: A short pass with blockers out in front.
entries.full: Linemen let rushers through, then release downfield to block for a short throw behind the rush.

entries.kid: A run wide around the end.
entries.full: A perimeter run to the edge, often with pulling linemen leading the back.

entries.kid: 3 linemen and 4 linebackers.
entries.full: A front with three down linemen (nose and two ends) and four linebackers; the outside linebackers are usually the edge rushers.

entries.kid: Hurrying to score before time runs out.
entries.full: The offense's hurry-up mode at the end of a half: quick plays, sideline throws, timeouts and spikes to stop the clock.

entries.kid: Each defender guards an area of the field.
entries.full: Each defender is responsible for an area and covers whoever enters it, with eyes on the quarterback.

entries.kid: A front that covers the center and both guards.
entries.full: A 0-technique nose and two 3-techniques (the front of the 46 defense), so no interior lineman can release cleanly to a linebacker.

entries.kid: Sending extra rushers.
entries.full: Rushing five or more, typically adding a linebacker or defensive back; stunts (twists) swap linemen's paths instead.

entries.kid: Man coverage with no deep safety.
entries.full: Every defender in coverage plays man with no deep help, usually with extra rushers; beaten by quick throws and hot routes.

entries.kid: Man coverage with one deep safety.
entries.full: Man coverage underneath with a single free safety in the deep middle, often with a 'rat' or 'robber' defender; attacked with crossers and rubs.

entries.kid: Two safeties split the deep field in halves.
entries.full: Two deep halves, corners squat in the flats, five underneath zones; weak in the deep middle and behind the corner (smash).

entries.kid: Three defenders each guard a deep third.
entries.full: Corners and the free safety take deep thirds with four underneath; stressed by four verticals and seam routes.

entries.kid: Four defenders each guard a deep quarter.
entries.full: Corners and safeties take deep quarters, with safeties reading the slot and fitting the run; softer underneath.

entries.kid: Groups of coverages that look alike.
entries.full: Man (Cover 0, 1) and zone (Cover 2, 3, 4) families, each with known weaknesses that pass concepts target.

entries.kid: A curl with a flat route underneath.
entries.full: A high-low read on the flat defender; with the stick concept, a staple of the quick game.

entries.kid: The side the offense leans to.
entries.full: Usually the tight end's side (run strength); against spread sets, often the side with more receivers (passing strength). Fronts and coverages set to it.

entries.kid: Four receivers go deep.
entries.full: Four vertical routes, two up the seams, against three or fewer deep defenders.

entries.kid: The spaces between blockers.
entries.full: Lettered from the center out: A (center-guard), B (guard-tackle), C (tackle-tight end), D (outside the tight end).

entries.kid: A run aimed at one designed hole.
entries.full: Power, counter, trap and duo: down blocks, kick-outs, pullers or double teams build a specific hole.

entries.kid: Two shallow crossers passing each other.
entries.full: Two receivers crossing at shallow depth to create traffic against man coverage and sit in zone holes.

entries.kid: A gap run with a pulling guard.
entries.full: Playside down blocks, a kick-out on the end, and the backside guard pulling through the hole for the linebacker.

entries.kid: Tackling the quarterback before he throws.
entries.full: A tackle of the passer behind the line of scrimmage on a pass play; with hits and hurries, part of 'pressure'.

entries.kid: A hitch under a corner route.
entries.full: A high-low on the flat corner: hitch underneath, corner route over him; a classic Cover 2 beater.

entries.kid: A number for where a lineman lines up.
entries.full: Alignment numbers: 0 head-up center, 1 shade on the center, 2 head-up guard, 3 guard's outside shoulder, 4 head-up tackle, 4i tackle's inside shoulder, 5 tackle's outside shoulder; numbers past 5 differ by system.

entries.kid: Defensive ends lined up very wide.
entries.full: Ends aligned well outside the tight ends for a running start at the passer, at the cost of wider interior running lanes.

entries.kid: A deep crossing route behind clear-outs.
entries.full: The Y receiver runs a deep cross behind the linebackers while outside routes clear the deep defenders; a Cover 3 beater.

entries.kid: A run where linemen block areas and the back picks the hole.
entries.full: Inside and outside zone: linemen step together, combine and climb; the back reads the blocks to hit, bounce or cut back.

entries.kid: Linebackers blitzing through the gaps beside the center.
entries.full: Double A-gap mugs and cross dogs: linebackers threatening or attacking the interior gaps to collapse the pocket.

entries.kid: A defense with six defensive backs.
entries.full: Six defensive backs, typically against four receivers or on long passing downs; package names beyond dime vary by staff.

entries.kid: A five-man blitz with zone coverage behind it.
entries.full: Five rushers with three deep and three underneath zones, often with a lineman dropping into coverage.

entries.kid: Plays from just outside the end zone.
entries.full: Short-yardage situations at the goal line, usually with heavy personnel on both sides.

entries.kid: A quick throw when a blitzer is unblocked.
entries.full: When rushers outnumber blockers, the quarterback throws quickly to a receiver breaking into the space the blitzer left.

entries.kid: A receiver running across the formation before the snap.
entries.full: Jet motion crosses in front of the quarterback at full speed at the snap; orbit motion loops behind him.

entries.kid: Keeping extra players in to block.
entries.full: Seven or eight blockers with two or three receivers in the route: more time, fewer targets.

entries.kid: Naming the middle linebacker to set blocking.
entries.full: The pre-snap identification of a 'Mike' that sets every blocker's assignment in pass protection.

entries.kid: The quarterback reads a defender instead of blocking him.
entries.full: Plays that leave one defender unblocked and let the quarterback choose (give, keep, pitch) based on what he does: zone read, speed option, triple option.

entries.kid: Faking a run before passing.
entries.full: A run fake that draws linebackers and safeties forward before a pass behind them; includes bootlegs that roll away from the fake.

entries.kid: Inside the opponent's 20-yard line.
entries.full: The area inside the opponent's 20, where the field is compressed and scoring touchdowns rather than field goals decides games.

entries.kid: A run play with a quick pass option.
entries.full: Run-pass option: the line run-blocks while the quarterback reads a conflict defender after the snap and hands off or throws a quick route.

entries.kid: Blitzes that out-number one side or hide who's rushing.
entries.full: An overload sends more rushers to one side than it can block; a creeper (simulated pressure) rushes four from unexpected spots while dropping a lineman.

entries.kid: The line slides one way to block.
entries.full: Linemen block zones by sliding together to one side while a back takes the edge rusher on the other.

entries.kid: How far apart players line up.
entries.full: The spacing between linemen or receivers; wide splits stretch a defense, tight splits create traffic, rubs and blocking angles.

entries.kid: Snapping the ball fast without a huddle.
entries.full: No-huddle speed that limits defensive substitution, disguise and complex calls; also a clock tool.

entries.kid: Hand off or keep, based on one unblocked defender.
entries.full: Inside zone with the backside end left unblocked; if he crashes on the back, the quarterback keeps; if he stays, the quarterback gives.

entries.kid: How many defenders are near the line.
entries.full: The number of defenders in the box compared with the offense's blockers; more blockers favours the run, more defenders the pass.

entries.kid: Quarters to one side, Cover 2 to the other.
entries.full: Quarter-quarter-half: quarters to one side of the formation and halves (Cover 2) to the other.

entries.kid: A route the receiver chooses after the snap.
entries.full: A route that breaks away from man leverage or settles in a zone window, read by both the receiver and the quarterback.

entries.kid: Zone coverage that turns into man as routes develop.
entries.full: Zone rules that convert to man once routes declare; quarters (with variations such as palms) is the classic example. Rules and names vary by staff.

entries.kid: Rules that differ between the pros and college.
entries.full: Examples: two feet in for an NFL catch (one in college); NFL runners must be touched down; narrower NFL hash marks; NFL pass interference is a spot foul (college: up to 15 yards).

entries.kid: The order a quarterback reads his receivers.
entries.full: The sequence of reads on a pass play: hot (against a blitz), first, second and third reads, then the checkdown.

entries.kid: Cover 2 with the middle linebacker running deep.
entries.full: Cover 2 in which the Mike linebacker carries the deep middle, closing the hole between the safeties.

entries.kid: Man coverage with two deep safeties.
entries.full: Man coverage underneath with two safeties splitting the deep field in halves, letting corners play tight.

entries.kid: Two defenders on one receiver.
entries.full: Doubling one receiver with an under and an over defender, often from a normal-looking shell.

entries.kid: Choosing the coverage at the line.
entries.full: Calling two coverages and picking one at the line from the formation or motion, sometimes with colour codes (red/green) or one-word calls against tempo.

entries.kid: A corner pretends to play deep, then jumps a short route.
entries.full: A corner shows deep-third depth, sinks at the snap to invite an outside throw, then drives on the flat or out with a safety covering deep behind him.
